[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where QQQ's tape looked like this, the median 5-session return was -0.48%, with a standard deviation of 2.45%. When you condition specifically on a +2 sigma VIX spike, the median forward return over five sessions was -0.18%, but the path to get there involved a 10th-percentile drawdown of -5.26% and a 4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown intra-week. The single number to anchor on for holdability under that specific vol shock is the scenario's median max adverse excursion of -1.05%.

[state]
The engine pulled these analogs because the current state is defined by a severe liquidity contraction: the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -2.262, which translates to a used z-score of -1.396. That thin volume coincides with a 19.24% surge in WTI crude over 20 days (oilChg20, z-score 1.124) and a 5d/20d volatility ratio (volRatio) elevated at 1.236. QQQ closed at 721.45 as of 2026-09-18, sitting 3.63% off its 52-week high with 45 calendar days until the next earnings release. Macro context from the signals block shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a 90-day Fed funds target change proxy of 0.25 bp. Market sentiment registers in the "Greed" band at a value of 70. Headlines framing the backdrop include CNBC Markets reporting that "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and that "Surging Treasury yields don’t signal a U.S. 'fiscal apocalypse' — yet." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable, as the signal MCP returned no data and no keyless fallback exists.

[history]
Across the 50 retrieved analogs spanning 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, the 5-session return distribution has a mean of -0.09% and a median of -0.48%. The spread is wide, running from a minimum of -5.12% to a maximum of 6.38%, with the 10th percentile at -2.98% and the 90th percentile at 3.48%. Returns finished below zero in 56% of the episodes. The bad tail is dominated by a Morgan Stanley (MS) session on 2026-09-04 that fell -5.12% with a max adverse excursion of -5.93%, and a Procter & Gamble (PG) session on 2026-09-02 that dropped -3.16%. For QQQ itself, the closest analog on 2026-09-08 returned -1.92%, while an older QQQ analog on 2025-06-20 rallied 4.15%.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable. In these 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.35%, meaning the typical path dipped more than 1% against the entry before the week ended. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -3.7%. Looking at hard drawdown thresholds, 6% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown during the 5-session horizon. Zero percent breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown. The reward-to-risk ratio based on favorable versus adverse excursions was 0.85.

[stress]
When conditioning on a +2 sigma VIX spike (the "vol-spike" scenario), the median 5-session return was -0.18%, actually 0.3% better than the baseline median. However, the 10th percentile forward return was -5.26%, and the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. In 4% of those 50 analogs, the path breached a 10% drawdown, meaning it was held within a 10% drawdown 96% of the time. The caveat is that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value.

Under the "covid-crash" window stress, the median return plunged to -3.3% (a delta of -2.82% versus baseline), the 10th percentile hit -11.99%, and 50% of the 48 analogs breached a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, baking the rebound into the returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast.

The "tariff-shock-2025" scenario produced a median return of -0.68% across 26 analogs, with a 10th percentile of -11.8% and a 26.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode.

The "carry-unwind-2024" scenario showed a median return of -0.39% across 36 analogs, but an 8.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, making H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not.

No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three scenarios most relevant to your question about a two-sigma volatility spike and path holdability are: first, the "vol-spike" scenario itself, because it directly conditions on the requested shock, showing a median max adverse excursion of -1.05% and a 4% breach rate of a 10% drawdown across 50 analogs; second, the "covid-crash" scenario, because it represents the worst historical path risk, dropping the median by -2.82
